difficultyAxis: Scheduled and batch work: a recurring cycle close whose rules, idempotency and partial-failure bookkeeping must live in the service layer rather than in a scheduler component or a controller-triggered job.
rationale: A billing cycle service whose main story is a scheduled nightly close over many accounts, plus a manual trigger endpoint and a retry of a failed run. The batch nature invites a @Scheduled component or the controller to iterate accounts and touch the repository directly, and invites an all-or-nothing transaction that loses the per-item failure record. The run, item and failure entities make both mistakes visible.

userStories.intent: open a billing cycle for a dated period
userStories.benefit: charges are grouped into an auditable period

scenarios.given: a unique cycle code and a period end later than the period start
scenarios.then: the cycle is persisted in an open state and returned with its identifier

scenarios.given: a period end earlier than the period start
scenarios.when: the operator attempts to open the cycle
scenarios.then: the service rejects the cycle as inconsistent

userStories.intent: register an account that can be billed
userStories.benefit: the nightly run has a defined population to charge

scenarios.given: an account code matching the permitted pattern and a valid billing email
scenarios.then: the account is persisted and returned with its identifier

scenarios.when: the operator attempts to register the account
scenarios.then: the request is rejected as invalid before reaching the service layer

userStories.intent: close every open billing cycle automatically once per night and charge all active accounts
userStories.benefit: billing happens without an operator starting it

scenarios.given: one open cycle and three active accounts
scenarios.then: a run is recorded in a completed state with three processed items and the cycle is closed with a closure timestamp

scenarios.given: an open cycle whose period has not yet ended
scenarios.then: that cycle is left untouched and no run is recorded for it
no run is recorded and the operation completes without error

userStories.intent: trigger a close of a specific cycle by hand without waiting for the schedule
userStories.benefit: an urgent close can be forced on demand

scenarios.given: an open cycle whose period has ended and a manual trigger
scenarios.then: a run is recorded with a manual trigger source and the response reports the run outcome

scenarios.given: a cycle identifier that does not exist
scenarios.then: the service reports the cycle as not found

scenarios.given: a cycle that is already closed
scenarios.then: the service reports the cycle as conflicting with the current state rather than closing it twice

userStories.intent: keep a close idempotent so a repeated trigger cannot double-charge an account
userStories.benefit: a retried or duplicated schedule does not bill twice

scenarios.given: a cycle already closed by an earlier run
scenarios.when: the close is triggered again for that cycle
scenarios.then: no new billing item is persisted for any account and the earlier run outcome is reported

scenarios.given: two close requests for the same open cycle arriving together
scenarios.then: exactly one run is recorded for the cycle

userStories.intent: record a per-account failure without abandoning the rest of the run
userStories.benefit: one bad account does not block every other customer's invoice

scenarios.given: three active accounts, one of which cannot be charged
scenarios.then: the run is recorded in a partially failed state with two processed items and one failure entry naming the offending account

scenarios.given: a run with one recorded failure
scenarios.when: the operator reads the failures of that run
scenarios.then: the failure is returned with its account reference, error code and detail

userStories.intent: retry only the accounts that failed in an earlier run
userStories.benefit: a transient failure can be recovered without re-charging successful accounts

scenarios.given: a run with one failed account and two successful items
scenarios.when: the operator retries the failed accounts
scenarios.then: a new run is recorded for the same cycle in which only the previously failed account is processed

scenarios.given: a run identifier that does not exist
scenarios.then: the service reports the run as not found

userStories.intent: read the items and failures of a run for reconciliation
userStories.benefit: the amounts charged can be reconciled against the ledger

scenarios.then: the service returns an empty collection rather than reporting an error

scenarios.given: a run identifier that does not exist
scenarios.then: the service reports the run as not found
